transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

They sent me over from the station. I guess I was... arranging the airway bags a certain way, and saying dispatch numbers out loud. My lieutenant told me to stop, but I couldn’t really step away. It felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would go bad.
Did you feel like you had to arrange the airway bags in that specific way?
Yeah. I mean... it wasn’t just how I wanted them. It felt like they had to be that way. The pattern was right, and if I stopped or messed it up, it felt like the whole bay would go bad.
Do you find yourself doing things like arranging objects or repeating actions outside of work as well?

I don’t know… mostly it was at the station. The airway bags, the dispatch numbers. I kept putting them in the pattern and saying the numbers, and I couldn’t really stop when he told me to. It felt like if I stepped away, the bay would go bad.
Do you have thoughts or urges like the one about the airway bags that happen to you when you're not at work?

Not really… I mean, it was mostly there, at the station. The airway bags, the numbers. I just knew the pattern was right, and if I stopped, it felt like the bay would go bad. I don’t know about outside work.
Did you feel like arranging the airway bags in that specific way was something you wanted to do, or did it feel like something you couldn't control?

It didn’t feel like just wanting to. I… I felt like I couldn’t stop it. The bags had to be in that pattern, and if I broke the sequence or stepped away when my lieutenant told me to, it felt like the whole bay would go bad.
Do you have disturbing or recurring thoughts that bother you when you're not at work?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed that… not outside work, I guess. Nothing I can name.
Have you ever felt like you had to perform a specific ritual or behavior when you're not at work?
I don’t think so. Not that I can really point to… it was more tied to work, from what I remember.
Do you have any habits or behaviors that you feel compelled to do when you're not at work?
Not really. I mean… I have routines, I guess, like anybody, but nothing I feel forced to do. Not that I’ve noticed.
Do you feel anxious or uncomfortable when things are not done in a specific order or way?

Yeah… mostly at work. If the bags weren’t set a certain way, or the numbers weren’t said right, it felt… wrong. Like I couldn’t just leave it. My lieutenant told me to stop and I still didn’t, because it felt like the bay would go bad if I broke it.
Do you feel like the airway bags or other things need to be arranged in a symmetrical or perfect way?
Yeah… the airway bags, mostly. I kept moving them into this pattern that felt right. I don’t know if it was “perfect,” but if it wasn’t that way, I couldn’t really step away.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind when you're not at work?
Not really… not that I can pin down. My mind gets busy sometimes, but I don’t know if I’d call it repeating thoughts.
Did arranging the airway bags in that specific way feel like something that was a part of you, or did it feel alien or against your will?

It didn’t feel… alien exactly. It felt like something I had to do. Like I knew that pattern was the right one, and if I stopped or broke the sequence, the whole bay would go bad. Even when my lieutenant told me to stop, I couldn’t really step away.
Do you think you would have felt the need to arrange the airway bags in that specific way if you were doing something similar outside of work?

I don’t know. It was mostly at the station… with the airway bags and the bay. Maybe if it was the same kind of setup, I might feel it, but I can’t really say. It was like if I didn’t keep the sequence, something there would go bad.
Do you think the need to arrange things in a specific way or repeat certain actions would happen in other situations or places outside of your work at the station?

I… I don’t really know. It was at the station, mostly. The airway bags, the dispatch numbers… that setup. I kept putting them in the pattern and saying the numbers because it felt like if I stopped, the bay would go bad. I haven’t really noticed it the same way other places.
Do you think you would feel the need to arrange things in a specific way if you were in a completely different environment?

I’m not sure. It really happened at the station… the airway bags, the dispatch numbers, the bay. I knew the pattern was right there, and if I broke it, it felt like everything would go bad. Somewhere totally different… I don’t know.
Do you think you would feel the need to arrange things in a specific way if you were doing a similar task at home?

Maybe… if it was like the same kind of thing. I don’t really do airway bags at home. At the station I just knew the pattern was right, and if I didn’t keep it or if I stepped away, it felt like the whole bay would go bad. At home, I’m not sure.
Do you think you could be triggered to arrange things in a specific way in a situation that is not related to your work at the station?

I don’t know… maybe if it felt like there was a sequence I had to keep. At the station it was the airway bags and the dispatch numbers. I kept moving them into the pattern and saying the numbers, and I couldn’t step away when they told me to. It felt like if I broke it, the whole bay would go bad.
Do you think your need to arrange things in a specific way is only triggered by things related to your work at the station?

I guess… mostly, yeah. It’s really been the station. The airway bags, the dispatch numbers… I had to keep them in the right sequence. When my lieutenant told me to stop, I couldn’t, because it felt like the bay would go bad if I broke it.
Do you think you would feel the need to arrange things in a specific way if you were in a situation that has nothing to do with your job as a firefighter?

I don’t really know. It’s mostly been at the station… with the airway bags and the dispatch numbers. I kept putting them in the pattern and saying the numbers, and I couldn’t stop when my lieutenant told me. It felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would go bad.
Have you ever experienced significant distress or impairment in your daily life due to your need to arrange things in a specific way or repeat certain actions?

Yeah… it’s been a problem. I’m not on the ambulance anymore, and even the desk stuff—notes, equipment checks—I couldn’t keep it reliable enough, so they took me off the schedule.

And at home… I don’t really keep up with things like I used to. I don’t see people much. Friends, I mean. It’s… yeah, it’s gotten in the way.
